title: SIA Urges Tighter Oversight of Automated License Plate Readers
summary: The Security Industry Association issued policy recommendations urging stronger privacy safeguards, retention limits, access controls, audits, and misuse prohibitions for ALPR systems, while defending the technology's public safety value. The article situates the recommendations against growing pushback on Flock Safety and notes Flock's recent changes, including reducing default retention from 30 to seven days and mandating audit and MFA features.

key_quotes.quote: ALPR is not — and must never become — a tool for mass surveillance or tracking law-abiding citizens
ALPR outputs are investigative leads only, not conclusive evidence, and must not serve as the sole basis for action without human verification
Secure Justice has recorded 214 cities and counties that have dropped Flock since 2021, including 93 jurisdictions in August alone
